exposure: increased echogenicity in the ganglionic eminence (GE)
Abnormal ultrasound findings (increased echogenicity in the ganglionic eminence, cyst in the ganglionic eminence, subependymal cyst, slight lateral ventricular enlargement)
outcome: Incidence of NRI, RIAC, feeding hypoxemia, and RIGER
Association between different types of NRI
Frequency and severity of feeding hypoxemia
Need for additional feeding control after discharge
cohort: Infants weighing at least 2000 g and born at a gestational age of at least 36 weeks
finding: Neonatal respiratory inhibition (NRI) was observed in approximately 50% of infants, with feeding hypoxemia being the most common type, and was associated with various perinatal factors and maternal conditions.
mod_finding: While the study notes cesarean section as a potential perinatal factor related to neonatal respiratory inhibition, it doesn't directly compare outcomes between different modes of delivery.
